name: eddy-ios
//overrides: react-dom is never declared with a version anywhere in this tree — expo,
expo-router, @expo/metro-runtime and @rnmapbox/maps all peer-depend on it
as "*". npm auto-installs peers, so it resolves the NEWEST react-dom, and
every react-dom past 19.2.3 peer-requires a react past the 19.2.3 that Expo
SDK 57 pins. That is an ERESOLVE deadlock on a plain `npm install`, and it
is why this project could only be installed with --legacy-peer-deps — which
silently skips peer installation and drops react-native-reanimated,
react-native-gesture-handler and react-native-worklets out of the tree.
$react tracks the direct react dependency rather than restating 19.2.3, so
the next Expo SDK bump moves both together and this cannot drift.
react-dom is NOT added as a real dependency: nothing in this app renders to
the DOM. It is here only to constrain something else's peer.
//typegen: app.json sets experiments.typedRoutes, so expo-router generates the union
of every route into .expo/types/router.d.ts, and tsconfig.json includes it.
.expo/ is gitignored, so that declaration is a BUILD ARTIFACT with no
committed copy — and until this script existed, nothing but the dev server
ever wrote one. That made the two environments disagree in opposite
directions: a laptop typechecked against whatever its last `expo start`
left behind, so a route added since read as invalid; CI had no declaration
at all, so Href degraded to something permissive and route errors could not
fire there. Running it before tsc gives both the same, current answer.
`expo customize tsconfig.json` looks unrelated and is not. It is the
supported entry point into the CLI's type generation without a dev server
or Metro (@expo/cli's own comment in start/server/type-generation/routes.ts
names this command as the case that reaches it), and it regenerates the
declaration from the current contents of app/ — additions and deletions
both. `expo export` does NOT, which is what an earlier attempt at this
assumed and why it was reverted.
It also rewrites tsconfig.json and expo-env.d.ts to what Expo wants. That
is the same side effect `expo start` already has, and both are idempotent
here, so it leaves the tree clean — but a tsconfig diff after a typecheck
is this, not you.
